beats.narration_text: Two companies report the same thing, revenue, and label it completely differently. A human sees they mean the same thing in a second. Software cannot assume that.

props.command: How do two companies report the same thing?

Net Sales · Revenue from Contracts · a custom tag.
The software must decide when they mean the same thing.

beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Asavari, a fellow at Humanitarians AI. This video is about a deceptively hard problem in financial data: two companies reporting the same thing under different names. You'll learn how to decide, and prove, when two differently-labeled numbers actually mean the same thing. If you ever combine data from different sources, this one's for you.

props.command: What is this video about, and why should I watch it?
props.topic: HUMANITARIANS AI · MYCROFT — SEC FILINGS AGENT
output: Who: Asavari, a Humanitarians AI fellow
Why watch: catch the mistake before it costs you

beats.narration_text: Three filings, three different labels, all pointing at the same idea. Treat them as different and your comparison across companies is broken. Treat them as the same without checking and you might merge two things that only look alike. Either mistake is silent.

artifactLines: smpl: custom extension  ->  all mean: revenue

beats.narration_text: The fix is deliberate. For each metric, keep an ordered list of tags, most preferred first, the modern standard before the older ones. Take the first the company reports, and record which tag matched, on every value. So the mapping is visible and anyone can disagree. And when nothing matches, it doesn't guess. It flags the metric as missing.

props.title: resolve_metric
props.code:
candidates = [
  'RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax',  # ASC 606
  'Revenues',
  'SalesRevenueNet',            # legacy
]
for tag in candidates:
    if tag in facts: return match(tag)   # record WHICH tag
return MISSING   # never guessed

beats.narration_text: One nuance. When a company uses its own custom tag, that's not an error. It's often the most accurate label for something unusual. So missing doesn't mean bad data. It means the tool needs a human to confirm the mapping. That distinction keeps the dataset honest.

props.artifactTitle: A custom tag isn't a wrong tag
artifactLines: It just isn't in the standard list
'Missing' means 'needs a human mapping', not 'bad data'

beats.narration_text: Any time you merge data from different sources, comparability is a decision, and you should be able to prove it. Do the labels truly mean the same thing? Which exact source did each value come from? Could someone audit that mapping later? And what did you refuse to merge? Numbers are never just numbers. The names matter.

props.artifactTitle: Comparability is a decision you have to prove
props.artifactHeading: Same name is not the same as same meaning
